On the occasion of the 500th anniversary of the university, [Albert Einstein](/wiki/Albert_Einstein "Albert Einstein") and [Max Planck](/wiki/Max_Planck "Max Planck") received honorary doctorates on 12 November 1919. This made the University of Rostock the world's first institute of higher learning to award this honour to Einstein. The doctorate was not revoked during the [Nazi rule](/wiki/Nazi_Germany "Nazi Germany") in Germany (1933–1945), despite such orders by the Nazis. The reason for this remains unknown. Psychologist [David Katz](/wiki/David_Katz_(psychologist) "David Katz (psychologist)") and professor of dentistry and dean of the medical faculty [Hans Moral](/w/index.php?title=Hans_Moral&action=edit&redlink=1 "Hans Moral (page does not exist)") lost their posts in 1933 among others.

The end of the [Second World War](/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War") in 1945 brought many changes. The university, now finding itself in the Soviet Zone of Germany (the later [German Democratic Republic](/wiki/German_Democratic_Republic "German Democratic Republic")), was re-opened on 24 February 1946. The Faculty of Law was closed in 1951, a Faculty of Agriculture was introduced in 1950 and in 1951 saw the opening of a Department of Shipbuilding (renamed Faculty of Technology in 1963). The University of Rostock was the first traditional university in Germany to open a technical faculty. In 1952, the Faculty of Aviation was opened, but eventually relocated to [Dresden](/wiki/Dresden "Dresden").

In 1976 the university was renamed Wilhelm-Pieck-Universität after [Wilhelm Pieck](/wiki/Wilhelm_Pieck "Wilhelm Pieck"), the first president of the [German Democratic Republic](/wiki/German_Democratic_Republic "German Democratic Republic"). The renaming was annulled after the [German reunification](/wiki/German_reunification "German reunification").

Main article: [Soviet Moonshot](/wiki/Soviet_crewed_lunar_programs "Soviet crewed lunar programs")

Soviet leader [Nikita Khrushchev](/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev "Nikita Khrushchev") said in October 1963 the USSR was "not at present planning flight by cosmonauts to the Moon," while insisting that the Soviets had not dropped out of the race. Only after another year did the USSR fully commit itself to a Moon-landing attempt, which ultimately failed.

At the same time, Kennedy had suggested various joint programs, including a possible Moon landing by Soviet and U.S. astronauts and the development of better weather-monitoring satellites, eventually resulting in the [Apollo-Soyuz mission](/wiki/Apollo-Soyuz_mission "Apollo-Soyuz mission"). Khrushchev, sensing an attempt by Kennedy to steal Russian space technology, rejected the idea at first: if the USSR went to the Moon, it would go alone. Though Khrushchev was eventually warming up to the idea, the realization of a joint Moon landing was choked by Kennedy's assassination.[[56]](#cite_note-Launius_2019_pp._167–168-56)

[Sergey Korolev](/wiki/Sergey_Korolev "Sergey Korolev"), the [Soviet space program](/wiki/Soviet_space_program "Soviet space program")'s chief designer, had started promoting his [Soyuz](/wiki/Soyuz_(spacecraft) "Soyuz (spacecraft)") craft and the [N1](/wiki/N1_(rocket) "N1 (rocket)") launcher rocket that would have the capability of carrying out a human Moon landing. Khrushchev directed Korolev's design bureau to arrange further space firsts by modifying the existing Vostok technology, while a second team started building a completely new launcher and craft, the Proton booster and the Zond, for a human cislunar flight in 1966. In 1964 the new Soviet leadership gave Korolev the backing for a Moon landing effort and brought all crewed projects under his direction.

A [four-sided die](/wiki/Four-sided_die "Four-sided die") and [pyramorphix](/wiki/Pyramorphix "Pyramorphix")

The [Royal Game of Ur](/wiki/Royal_Game_of_Ur "Royal Game of Ur"), dating from 2600 BC, was played with a set of tetrahedral dice. Especially in [roleplaying](/wiki/Roleplaying "Roleplaying"), this solid is known as a [4-sided die](/wiki/4-sided_die "4-sided die"), one of the more common [polyhedral dice](/wiki/Polyhedral_dice "Polyhedral dice"), with the number rolled appearing around the bottom or on the top vertex. Some [Rubik's Cube](/wiki/Rubik%27s_Cube "Rubik's Cube")-like puzzles are tetrahedral, such as the [Pyraminx](/wiki/Pyraminx "Pyraminx") and [Pyramorphix](/wiki/Pyramorphix "Pyramorphix").

[Stanley Kubrick](/wiki/Stanley_Kubrick "Stanley Kubrick") originally intended the [monolith](/wiki/Monolith_(Space_Odyssey) "Monolith (Space Odyssey)") in *[2001: A Space Odyssey](/wiki/2001:_A_Space_Odyssey_(film) "2001: A Space Odyssey (film)")* to be a tetrahedron, according to [Marvin Minsky](/wiki/Marvin_Minsky "Marvin Minsky"), a cognitive scientist and expert on [artificial intelligence](/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence") who advised Kubrick on the [HAL 9000](/wiki/HAL_9000 "HAL 9000") computer and other aspects of the movie. Kubrick scrapped the idea of using the tetrahedron when a viewer who saw footage of it did not recognize what it was, and he did not want anything in the film that regular people did not understand.[[37]](#cite_note-38)

The tetrahedron with regular faces is a solution to an old puzzle asking to form four equilateral triangles using six unbroken matchsticks.

[Arinobu Fukuhara](/wiki/Arinobu_Fukuhara "Arinobu Fukuhara") (1848–1924), the founder of Shiseido

The name *Shiseido* comes from a passage in the Chinese classic *[I Ching](/wiki/I_Ching "I Ching")* (Book of Changes) meaning "praise the virtues of the earth which nurtures new life and brings forth significant values".[[7]](#cite_note-7)[[8]](#cite_note-8)[[9]](#cite_note-9)

[Arinobu Fukuhara](/wiki/Arinobu_Fukuhara "Arinobu Fukuhara"), former head [pharmacist](/wiki/Pharmacist "Pharmacist") to the [Imperial Japanese Navy](/wiki/Imperial_Japanese_Navy "Imperial Japanese Navy"), established the Shiseido Pharmacy in 1872. After a visit to the United States and Europe, Arinobu added a [soda fountain](/wiki/Soda_fountain "Soda fountain") to the store. This later grew into the Shiseido Parlor restaurant business, and eventually led to the introduction of [ice cream](/wiki/Ice_cream "Ice cream") in Japan.

Arinobu passed on his company to his son, Shinzō Fukuhara, who became the company's second president in 1913. After Shinzō's experience traveling to Europe and the United States, he became interested in advertising as a large selling point for Shiseido which lead him to dedicate extensive resources to the company's design, much of which can be seen from product packaging and magazines from this time.[[10]](#cite_note-:0-10)

The energy released on the Earth's surface (*M*e, the energy magnitude, which is the *seismic potential for damage*) by the 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake was estimated at 1.1×1017 [joules](/wiki/Joules "Joules").[[49]](#cite_note-50)

The earthquake generated a seismic oscillation of the Earth's surface of up to 200–300 mm (8–12 in), equivalent to the effect of the [tidal forces](/wiki/Tides "Tides") caused by the Sun and Moon. The seismic waves of the earthquake were felt across the planet, as far away as the U.S. state of [Oklahoma](/wiki/Oklahoma "Oklahoma"), where vertical movements of 3 mm (0.12 in) were recorded. By February 2005, the earthquake's effects were still detectable as a 20 μm (0.02 mm; 0.0008 in) complex harmonic oscillation of the Earth's surface, which gradually diminished and merged with the incessant free oscillation of the Earth more than four months after the earthquake.[[50]](#cite_note-Virtanen-51)
